inputs.proposal: Bridge cleanup after the coalescing change: setSignalSet takes an opaque pointer, signal decode reads the standard 8-byte CAN payload, the staging buffer is rebuilt per frame, and dropped frames are reported from the GUI-side frame handler.

blockers: claim: Buffer size assumption: fixed 8-byte payload for CAN-FD signals, ignoring actual payload length; file: app/qttunebridge.cpp; quote: if (qttune_decode_signal(&def, frame->data, 8, &val) == 0) {
questions: Could qttune_frame_t::data_length ever exceed 64, leading to a buffer overrun when accessing frame->data?
Is the removal of the drop‑notification mechanism (notifyDropped) intentional, or will dropped frames never be reported to the UI?
Does the Entry struct in FrameListModel guarantee null‑termination of the name and unit fields, or should the code explicitly add a terminating NUL?

claim: Potential undefined behavior: strncpy does not null‑terminate destination strings for signal name and unit; file: app/qttunebridge.cpp; quote: strncpy(e.name, set->defs[i].name, sizeof(e.name) - 1);; quote2: strncpy(e.unit, set->defs[i].unit, sizeof(e.unit) - 1);
nits: Consider using std::string or QString for signal names and units to avoid manual strncpy and null‑termination issues.
The lambda capturing `copy` by value in `onFrame` copies the entire frame; if frame size grows, this could become a performance concern.
Ensure that `qttune_mock_signal_set()` returns a stable, thread‑safe pointer before it is passed to `setSignalSet`.
